findings.doc_quote: When old_state is None , returns False even if the attribute is present on the new state.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/predicates.py:530-531 — `if value.payload.data.old_state is None: return get_attr_new(self.attr_name)(value) is not MISSING_VALUE`
findings.explanation: When old_state is None, AttrDidChange returns True if the attribute is present on new_state and False only if it is absent. The class docstring (lines 521-524) says the same.
findings.suggested_fix: When old_state is None, returns True if the attribute is present on the new state (treated as changed), otherwise False.

findings.doc_quote: Returns True when the string value contains substring , ignoring case.
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/conditions.py:227 — `return isinstance(value, str) and self.substring in value`
findings.explanation: Contains is a plain, case-sensitive substring test. Nothing lowercases either side.
findings.suggested_fix: Returns True when the string value contains substring (case-sensitive).

findings.doc_quote: collection must be a sequence, not a string. Passing a string raises TypeError .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/conditions.py:121-122 — `if isinstance(collection, str): raise ValueError("collection must be a sequence of values, not a string")`
findings.explanation: _validate_collection raises ValueError, not TypeError. It is called from __post_init__ of IsIn, NotIn, Intersects and NotIntersects.

findings.doc_quote: Returns True when float(old) < threshold <= float(new) .
findings.explanation: The boundary inequalities are the other way round. A rise from exactly the threshold to above it counts as a crossing. A new value equal to the threshold does not. The doc also omits that boolean values never fire.
findings.suggested_fix: Returns True when float(old) <= threshold < float(new). A missing, non-numeric, or boolean value returns False.

findings.doc_quote: A missing or non-numeric value returns False .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/event_handling/conditions.py:642-643 — `if isinstance(old_value, bool) or isinstance(new_value, bool): return False`
findings.explanation: The formula on this line is correct. The description leaves out that boolean values also never fire. The same omission applies to CrossedAbove on line 104.
findings.suggested_fix: A missing, non-numeric, or boolean value returns False.

findings.doc_quote: Excludes last_reported , last_updated , and last_changed by default.
findings.explanation: The default exclusion list has a fourth entry, context. The doc also says the result maps changed keys to (old, new). In fact the result is a nested dict, with attributes nested under an "attributes" key.
findings.suggested_fix: Excludes last_reported, last_updated, last_changed, and context by default.

summary: Most of the page matches the code. Predicate signatures, accessor behavior, literal coercion, operator shorthand, and the Comparison ops all check out. The errors cluster in the Conditions section: Contains is not case-insensitive, the collection validation raises ValueError rather than TypeError, and CrossedAbove has the wrong inequality boundaries. Elsewhere, AttrDidChange gets the old_state=None behavior backwards, and the get_all_changes default exclude list is missing context.
